newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Some bids edge higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Some bids edge higher.

text.p: Some bids for spring wheat edged up again Tuesday as farmers continue to hold grain hoping for higher prices, merchandisers said.
"Movement was very quiet because everybody is convinced that the market is going higher," said one Montana-based dealer.
History-making flooding in the North Dakota and Minnesota generated concerns about spring wheat planting delays and acreage abandonment in those states.
Markets have responded with higher prices, and farmers were not even selling their new crop wheat, despite the recent sharp gains.
"They are still not biting at my new crop prices, which worries me a little bit," said one wheat dealer.
The merchandiser was bidding for new crop hard red winter wheat at $4.28 per bushel.
Cash prices for white wheat also jumped higher Monday.
"It's all weather related," said a dealer in the U.S. Northwest.
